newsitem.title: USA: Interior decorators charged with money-laundering.
newsitem.headline: Interior decorators charged with money-laundering.

text.p: Two interior decorators who allegedly bought expensive furnishings and art work for slain Colombian drug lord Jose Santacruz Londono have been arrested on charges of conspiring to launder $30 million, U.S. officials said on Thursday.

Anthony Blarek, 56, and Frank Pellecchia, 48, were arrested on Wednesday at their multi-million-dollar home in San Francisco's stylish Sea Cliff neighbourhood, the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration said.
The two men were being held without bail pending a hearing in federal court in San Francisco on Monday.

An indictment returned by a federal grand jury in New York charged the men with conspiring to launder $30 million of the cocaine fortunes of Santacruz, the third-ranking leader of the Cali cocaine cartel. The drug lord was shot and killed by Colombian police in March 1996, two months after escaping from jail. They were also charged with obstruction of justice.

The indictment seeks forfeiture of the San Francisco house, an East Hampton, New York, property, other real estate, bank accounts, safe deposit box contents and vehicles, all of which -- according to the U.S. government -- were bought with the proceeds of their work for Santacruz.

Blarek and Pellecchia both face sentences of up to 40 years in prison and fines of $60 million. A statement from federal prosecutors said the two men lived in the United States but did not say if they were American citizens.
The 29-page indictment alleged that Blarek and Pellecchia, partners in an interior design business based first in Miami and later in San Francisco, took Santacruz on as a client in about 1978.
After Congress passed laws targeting drug money-laundering in 1986, Blarek and Pellecchia continued to handle enormous sums of Santacruz's money, federal prosecutors said.

They travelled throughout the United States and the world, gathering expensive sculptures, paintings, decorative furniture and jewelry for Santacruz, they said. The items were shipped to false names or "straw men" in Colombia, the officials said.
The most recent project the interior decorators worked on was Santacruz's "Casa Blanca" in Cali, Colombia -- an $18 million replica of the White House in Washington, they said.

Blarek and Pellecchia received wire transfers from overseas bank accounts of up to $500,000 to finance the design, decoration and furnishing of the home, which boasts a vast central hall, a hair salon and huge dining and entertaining facilities, they said.
